items.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021
items.q: I’m a big Brecker fan... I kind of got more onto Brecker... I think those three. And then from there I kind of got more onto Brecker and Bob Berg.

ctx.x: might feel crappy, but you’re playing for the audience. You can’t necessarily afford, I’m not even sure how to put this into words, to play how you’re feeling. You’ve got to play well.

Right. Yeah. Absolutely. It’s something I think about a lot, one of my Australian teachers studied with Brecker back in the day. And a great bit of advice he told me was that Brecker said to him, “Well what you have to work on is having your bad day, your worst day, at a certain level you know. Your best day could be up here, but your worst day can’t be lower, it has to still be up to a certain level, your worst day.” That’s what you’ve got to work on. And I think about that a lot. I think we have to, you know,…

Back to this record for a moment, I was glad to see that, of course you were able to play with some really wonderful people here, but also that you had at least half the tunes were your own compositions. And from what I’ve learned a lot of times producers and so forth say well not too much of your own stuff right away, you need to play — people are going to read, “Oh yeah I like that song, I like that song, I’ll buy it.” So how did that happen?
